interview.name: Ira
interview.answer: I don’t have enough information in the notes to determine when or where the repair drive is being held.

reflections: Ira is responsive and follows through on commitments, especially when others confirm details.
Vik and Kira both rely on Ira for a simple status check, suggesting Ira is a dependable point of contact.
The group is coordinating around a repair drive through low-friction check-ins rather than firm plans.
Ira is consistently willing to help and follow up after errands, suggesting a cooperative, dependable role in the group.
Kira and others are checking for confirmation and expressing thanks, which points to a coordination-heavy situation where clarity matters.
Nell and Mina are relying on Ira to gather information from around the block, so Ira seems to be a useful go-between for the repair drive.
Ira is dependable and proactive, repeatedly offering to check around and report back after errands.
Mina, Nell, and Quinn are coordinating by sharing updates, expressing appreciation, and comparing notes on the repair drive.
The group communication is collaborative and practical, with people focusing on what still needs help and how to pass information along.
Ira is reliable and keeps others updated after errands, acting as a follow-up point for the repair drive.
Quinn is proactive and collaborative, quickly sharing the repair-drive list and offering to compare notes.
Gus is coordinating the in-person logistics for the community shed and is willing to bring extra tools to help.
Ira is the central coordinator and repeatedly reassures others with the same update, suggesting a dependable but repetitive communication style.
Rey and Eli are responsive helpers who want clear task lists before contributing, which points to a practical, coordination-focused relationship with Ira.
Gus is offering in-person support and extra tools, indicating the repair drive has some hands-on collaboration and shared responsibility.
